To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

perceptual learning of a visual motion direction discrimination task is associated with the sharpening of the tuning in MT and the enhancement of MT–IPS connectivity, both of which are consistent with the reweighting mechanism of perceptual learning.

perceptual learning of a motion direction discrimination in noise is associated with sharpened tuning of MT and strengthened connectivity between MT and IPS, and that the learning‐induced neural reorganization in MT and IPS persists for at least two weeks.

perceptual learning in motion direction discrimination task can be induced by training in noise, and that the neural correlates of learning can be observed in the sensory area (MT) and high‐level decision‐making area (IPS).

the neural mechanisms underlying motion perceptual learning are complex, and involve multiple cortical areas, including the motion‐specific areas, and the high‐order areas.

perceptual learning is a process that improves the efficiency of the neural system to extract the information of interest from noisy sensory signals, and it is achieved by the plasticity in sensory and decision‐making areas.
perceptual learning is the result of a complex interplay between the sensory cortex and higher‐order brain areas.

the brain is a plastic organ.
